text:
alex: Heads-up — we're seeing a lot of tiny fragments in the us-west-2 GPU pool again. Several pods got scheduled to nodes with only 1 free GPU slot left, leaving 2-3 GPUs stranded on other nodes. Cost and evictions spiking. Anyone else noticing this?

maya: yeah, noticed after the overnight batch. pod packing looks suboptimal when anti-affinity is set. Some of our low-priority jobs are pinned with nodeAffinity which blocks binpacking.

chris: can you paste a kube-scheduler log snippet? I wonder if the scoring favors spread over packing currently.

alex: here's a minimal dump from the scheduler around the time we saw failures:

```
I0312 02:14:08.123456 1 scheduler.go:424] pod "train-job-42" failed Fit for node "gpu-node-17": Insufficient resources: gpu: requested 2, available 1
I0312 02:14:08.123468 1 scheduler.go:430] Predicted score: node17=40, node19=60 (node19 chosen for spread)
I0312 02:14:08.123480 1 preemption.go:210] Preemption not attempted: low-priority and no suitable victims
```

maya: thanks. That Predicted score bit is interesting — seems like we still score for balanced distribution instead of minimizing free GPU fragments.

tim: quick note: autoscaler did trigger a small scale-up but nodes were cp-heavy so kubelet evicted a bunch of batch pods, making the fragmentation worse. infra-bot: we got a spike in spot evictions 02:15-02:20.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] scaleUp: requested 2 new instances in asg-gpu-usw2-1 at 02:16:02, capacity -> 28.

chris: three quick potential levers:
1) temporarily relax anti-affinity for best-effort / batch pools so scheduler can pack.
2) add a binpacking plugin or tweak priority function to prefer fewer nodes used (lower spread priority).
3) run a small eviction job targeting low-importance pods after scale-up to consolidate and free contiguous GPUs.

maya: I'm wary of changing affinity rules globally — that can affect performance isolation for Dedicated customers. What if we implement a scheduler predicate that only applies binpacking within the "batch-gpu" nodegroup? That keeps Dedicated pools untouched.

alex: +1 to scoped changes. Also we should add a metric: "gpu_fragmentation_ratio" per nodegroup and alert when >0.25 for 10m. Right now we only have GPU utilization and node count.

tim: I can add a prometheus query tomorrow:
```
(sum(node_gpu_free_gpus{nodegroup="us-west-2-gpu"}) / sum(node_gpu_total_gpus{nodegroup="us-west-2-gpu"}))
```
But fragmentation is more about distribution than total free. Maybe:
```
count(node_gpu_free_gpus{nodegroup="us-west-2-gpu"} == 1) / count(node_gpu_total_gpus{nodegroup="us-west-2-gpu"})
```
to catch lots of single free GPUs.

chris: good call. Also propose a cheap controller that watches pods in batch namespace and rewrites soft anti-affinity to prefer packing when GPU fragmentation exceeds threshold. Could be a short-lived feature flag.

maya: fine with a controller as an experiment. Who wants to own the PoC?

alex: I'll take the controller PoC with help from tim (metrics) and chris (scheduler tuning). Plan:
- PoC controller to rewrite soft anti-affinity labels (2d)
- Metric + Alert for fragmentation (1d)
- Scheduler config tweak for batch nodegroup (1d test)

chris: timeline sounds good. Keep Dedicated nodegroups untouched. If PoC reduces stranded GPUs and evictions, we'll add it to rollout.

tim: I'll add the prometheus rule and a grafana panel now. tagging: @maya @chris for visibility.

maya: thanks — also can we add a cost estimate for wasted GPU-hours last week? ops-finance asked. I can pull billing if needed.

alex: please do. rough estimate: ~120 GPU-hours stranded across 3 days in us-west-2 = ~12 GPU-days. we'll send to ops-finance.

chris: ping me once the metric is in, I'll simulate fragmentation locally by creating pods with nodeAffinity to specific nodes and test the controller. :gear:

alex: great. I'll create a minimal ticket and tag infra-sig. Closing this thread for now, will post updates in #eng-platform when PoC is up. :thumbsup:
